html:
SMTO-SSH-0008 — SMTO couldn't run this SSH command in a way it can safely track

GUID: c3fe31dd-e491-4cae-97cc-1f0d5f81417a
Slug: ssh-continuity-unsupported
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: ssh

What happened

  • SMTO checks every SSH command so it can recognize the remote computer next time. This command's setup didn't fit those checks, so SMTO stopped before running it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the command runs on a Gateway installed on Linux or macOS. You can see your Gateways in Settings › Setup › Gateways. SMTO can only check SSH connections made from Linux or macOS Gateways.
  2. Ask SMTO to run the SSH command on its own, without extra settings such as environment variables placed in front of it. SMTO only tracks a plain SSH command whose words it can match exactly.
  3. If this conversation has connected to the same computer before with a different key, continue in a new conversation by typing /new. When a conversation remembers two different keys for one computer, SMTO refuses to guess which one is right.

What success looks like

  • The SSH command runs and its output appears in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the SSH command you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to work around SMTO's SSH checks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway SSH observation rejected the request before execution: the Gateway is Windows, the shell command does not parse to the captured argv, environment overrides were supplied, the known setups are invalid or more than eight, or pinned host keys for the target are ambiguous.

What this means

  • Continuity observation rejects Windows, mismatched parsed argv, supplied environment overrides, malformed known setups or ambiguous pinned identity in its execution envelope. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • Continuity observation rejects Windows, mismatched parsed argv, supplied environment overrides, malformed known setups or ambiguous pinned identity in its execution envelope.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact command, argv, platform and known identities; a wrapper rejection may contain a more specific cause.

How to fix it

  • observe() in src/gateway_core/ssh_context.py requires a non-Windows Gateway, shlex.split(command) equal to the captured argv, no environment overrides, at most eight valid known setups and a single pinned fingerprint per target. Run ssh as a plain captured, non-interactive POSIX command without environment overrides; where continuity cannot be proven, use ordinary execution so OpenSSH establishes identity afresh. Do not bypass the check.
  • Use a supported captured POSIX Gateway and the existing SSH continuity envelope. Use ordinary execution when continuity cannot be proven.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported captured POSIX envelope validates, or ordinary supported execution establishes identity afresh.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
